• Hallstatt Skywalk for panoramic alpine views

Book a hotel directly in Hallstatt if your budget allows. Once the day trippers leave, the village becomes peaceful, quiet, and even more beautiful.

Please follow @journeysbysam for epic PTO-friendly adventures like this one! 🌍💼

🌟 Pikes Peak Guide
📍 Must-See Highlights:
🚗 Pikes Peak Highway – A winding 19-mile scenic road to the summit with jaw-dropping views all the way up!
🚂 Pikes Peak Cog Railway – America’s highest cog train perfect if you’d rather relax and enjoy the ride!
🥾 Devil’s Playground Trail – A challenging but rewarding hike starting above the treeline with insane alpine views.
☕ Summit House – Home to the famous high-altitude donuts (yes, they taste extra magical at 14,115 ft!).
📸 Summit Views – Panoramic views stretching from the Great Plains to the Rocky Mountains. Unreal!

💰 Entrance Fee:
🚗 $15 per adult | $50 per car (up to 5 people)
🚋 Cog Railway: Tickets start around $40–$60+ per person

✨ Tips for Visiting:
✅ Go early to avoid crowds and afternoon storms ⚡
✅ Dress in layers – it’s cold and windy at the top! 🧤
✅ Hydrate well – altitude sickness is real! 💧
✅ Book train tickets in advance – they sell out fast!
✅ Take your time driving – the views are just that good 😍

caption:
I spent days figuring out the shuttles, hikes and tourist traps so you don’t have to. Save this 📌

LAKE LOUISE, ALBERTA, Complete 2025/2026 Guide:

WHERE TO START: Everything starts at Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise. Parking is FULL by 4am in summer. You need Parks Canada shuttle. Moraine Lake is CLOSED to private cars, shuttle only.

BEST HIKES FROM THE LAKE (ranked):
1.  Lakeshore Trail - 4km flat, 1hr - SUNRISE spot, glass water
2.  Fairview Lookout - 2km, 100m gain - secret aerial view, no crowds
3.  Lake Agnes Tea House - 7.4km, 385m gain - famous tea house from 1905
4.  Plain of Six Glaciers - 13.8km, 587m gain - ends under Victoria Glacier, LESS CROWDED than Agnes
5.  Big Beehive - 10km, 650m gain - THE iconic shot straight down on the lake
6.  Devil’s Thumb - add-on from Beehive - 360° view, steep scramble

PRO TIP: Do the 25km Big Loop - Agnes > Beehive > Six Glaciers > Louise in one day if you’re fit.

MUST DO (non-hike):
•  Canoe Lake Louise at 8am - turquoise is brightest, no wind, red canoe photo

Rialto Beach in Olympic National Park feels like stepping into a moody coastal movie, towering sea stacks, massive driftwood, crashing Pacific waves and rugged Washington coastline in every direction.

Located near La Push on the Olympic Peninsula, Rialto Beach is one of the best beaches to visit in Washington State and a must-stop on any Olympic National Park road trip.

Walk along the shoreline toward Hole in the Wall, explore tide pools during low tide, photograph the dramatic sea stacks and stay for one of the most unforgettable sunsets on the Washington coast.

🌊 Check the tide schedule before hiking
🥾 Wear waterproof shoes with good grip
📸 Visit early morning or around sunset for dreamy light

November might just be the most magical month to revisit America’s most iconic landscapes and these three national parks are the ones I’ll never stop returning to.

Hi, I’m Sam, a Chicago based travel creator ✨ Here’s why Grand Canyon, Zion, and Lower Antelope Canyon keep pulling me back every single year.

🧡 Grand Canyon
November means cooler weather, fewer crowds, golden sunrise views, and hiking trails that feel calm and peaceful. Perfect for South Rim viewpoints, Bright Angel Trail, and dreamy photos without the summer rush.

💚 Zion National Park
The canyon walls glow deep red, the air is crisp, and trails like Angels Landing, Canyon Overlook, and Emerald Pools feel extra cinematic. Plus, easier parking, fewer lines, and cooler temps for hiking.

🧡 Lower Antelope Canyon
The soft November light inside the slot canyon is unreal. Smooth waves of sandstone, warm orange tones, and the kind of natural glow that makes every photo look edited (even when it’s not).

✨ Bonus: Horseshoe Bend
Just a quick stop from Page, AZ and November sunsets here are straight-up magic. Cooler weather + soft light = postcard views.

📍 Best Time to Visit in November
• Mild weather for hiking
• No harsh summer heat
• Smaller crowds + budget friendly stays
• Perfect golden hour lighting for photos
